svg.title: NTSB: a tanker's steering failed before it struck a docked riverboat in New Orleans
svg.desc: Editorial illustration. At midday on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, the towering dark bow of a tanker has struck the end of a small white multi-deck riverboat moored at a wharf; the riverboat is beginning to list. Behind the tanker a dashed wake curves sharply across the brown river, an illustrative trace of the steering failure that held its rudder to starboard, and its anchor chain runs down into the water. People in orange life vests hurry down the gangway and across the dock as a crew member waves them on; a harbor patrol boat and a tug approach. Steel cantilever bridge trusses cross the pale sky. It represents the NTSB's Nov. 15, 2026 preliminary finding about the Nov. 13 collision of the tanker Atlantic Asphalt with the riverboat American Heritage, in which everyone aboard survived.
